caveat: Mechanistic plausibility is not proof that this sauna protocol changes outcomes.

headline: NCCEH rapid review maps environmental and physiological hazards in sauna settings.
implication: Strong source for safety boundaries, cleaning, ventilation, signage, and high-risk-user exclusions.
caveat: Rapid review of hazards, not an efficacy study; directness varies by hazard type.

headline: Alberta public-pool standards set operational sauna temperature and monitoring requirements.
implication: Useful for safety operations, signage, clocks/timers, and upper-temperature guardrails.
caveat: Regulatory standard for public facilities; not a health-outcome study and not necessarily intended for private home sauna protocols.

headline: WHO guidance provides broad recreational-facility hazard-control context.
implication: Use as background for public facility hygiene and safety systems, not sauna-specific health effects.
caveat: WHO volume is about pools and similar environments; sauna-specific applicability is indirect.

headline: Post-exercise heat exposure does not clearly improve endurance performance beyond training.
implication: Avoid claiming endurance-performance benefits for the Finnish sauna protocol from this evidence base.
caveat: This is an exercise-coupled athlete/performance literature, not a sauna-only wellness protocol.

headline: Post-exercise heat exposure has mixed recovery and performance-adaptation evidence.
implication: Use this source to caution users who pair sauna with workouts and recovery goals.
caveat: Heterogeneity prevented meta-analysis and the source is not a sauna-only protocol trial.

headline: Fimea issues a warning: Wearing an opioid patch in the sauna may cause life-threatening poisoning — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use as a prominent hard-stop warning: do not use sauna with transdermal opioid patches; follow medical advice before heat exposure.
caveat: Regulatory warning and case surveillance, not an incidence study.; Focused on opioid patches, not all medications.

headline: Can I use a sauna or hot tub early in pregnancy? — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use as a clear pregnancy exclusion/caution source.
caveat: Patient guidance summary rather than a primary study.; Does not quantify sauna dose-risk threshold.

headline: Death in Sauna Associated With a Transdermal Fentanyl Patch — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use as a hard safety boundary: do not sauna with transdermal fentanyl/opioid patches unless explicit medical guidance says otherwise.
caveat: Single case report; cannot estimate absolute risk.; Specific to transdermal fentanyl/opioid patch context.

headline: Heat and Medications – Guidance for Clinicians — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use for medication-screening and heat-safety boundaries; not for efficacy.
caveat: General heat guidance, not sauna-specific clinical trial evidence.; Medication plan should be individualized with clinicians.

headline: Clinical Overview of Heat and Pregnancy — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use for pregnancy safety exclusion/caution and clinician-review language.
caveat: General heat/pregnancy guidance, not sauna-specific trial evidence.; Does not specify Finnish sauna dose thresholds.

headline: The effect of prescription and over-the-counter medications on core temperature in adults during heat stress: a systematic review and meta-analysis — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use for medication-class safety screening; do not turn heat-stress medication findings into sauna efficacy claims.
caveat: Not sauna-specific; heat-stress protocols varied.; Only 353 individuals and 16 women in extracted summary.

headline: Maternal hyperthermia and the risk for neural tube defects in offspring: systematic review and meta-analysis — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use as pregnancy safety evidence against routine sauna protocol use during pregnancy or possible early pregnancy without clinician guidance.
caveat: Hyperthermia sources include fever and other heat exposures, not only sauna.; Observational evidence; cannot establish exact sauna dose-risk threshold.

headline: Maternal heat exposure and neural tube defects — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use only as pregnancy/fetal-risk safety boundary; do not use for general adult efficacy or causality claims.
caveat: Observational exposure data with possible recall/confounding.; Sauna, hot tub, and fever exposures are not interchangeable with a controlled modern protocol.

headline: Heat exposure and drugs. A review of the effects of hyperthermia on pharmacokinetics — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use for broad medication heat-interaction framing; pair with newer medication guidance and specific opioid-patch warnings.
caveat: Narrative review; heterogeneous heat exposures and medications.; Older review predating newer heat-medication syntheses.

headline: Physical Activity and Exercise During Pregnancy and the Postpartum Period: ACOG Committee Opinion, Number 804 — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use only as pregnancy safety guidance; exclude from efficacy claims.
caveat: Exercise guideline, not sauna-specific protocol evidence.; Committee guidance rather than trial data.

headline: Effects of a Finnish sauna on the pharmacokinetics and haemodynamic actions of propranolol and captopril in healthy volunteers — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use as a concrete medication-screening source; avoid blanket claims across all drugs.
caveat: Small healthy-volunteer study.; Only specific drugs; not all beta-blockers or antihypertensives.

headline: In sporadic female sauna users, 80°C looked tolerable while 120°C created a clear safety boundary.
implication: Supports keeping beginners near conventional Finnish-sauna temperatures and avoiding extreme 120°C exposure.
caveat: Single-session female-student study; it does not test repeated 3x/week training or long-term outcomes.

headline: Heat stress and fetal risk. Environmental limits for exercise and passive heat stress during pregnancy: a systematic review with best evidence synthesis — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use as nuanced pregnancy heat-limit context; do not promote sauna use during pregnancy from it.
caveat: Systematic review of environmental limits, not a recommendation to prescribe sauna during pregnancy.; Sauna condition does not match hotter Finnish sauna or at-home behavior.

headline: Seminal and molecular evidence that sauna exposure affects human spermatogenesis — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use for a male-fertility caution: repeated hot sauna may temporarily impair spermatogenesis, especially relevant for people actively trying to conceive.
caveat: Very small male-only study.; Exposure was 2x/week for 3 months and not exactly the Murph 3x/week protocol.

headline: Same source reports fertility-marker worsening without cooling and lists practical contraindications.
implication: Supports cautious safety copy around male fertility, hydration/electrolytes, skin irritation, and medical exclusions.
caveat: Fertility findings are N-of-1 and cannot establish how testicular cooling changes risk or benefit.

headline: Older acute Finnish-sauna experiment documents strong physiological strain and adverse events at 80–90°C.
implication: Supports conservative session duration, stop rules, and avoidance of pushing to discomfort.
caveat: Older uncontrolled study with severe fixed exposure conditions; results should not be used to discourage all sauna use in healthy adults.

headline: Sudden-cardiac-death review supports cardiovascular context but keeps uncertainty visible.
implication: Helpful for safety and mortality-context language; not a basis for promising short-term Murph biomarker improvements.
caveat: Sudden cardiac death is not a protocol endpoint and the evidence is mainly observational.

headline: Benefits and risks of sauna bathing — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use as safety and contraindication context; keep older pregnancy/fertility statements explicitly qualified against newer guidance.
caveat: Narrative review, not a single controlled protocol trial.; Older safety statements can conflict with later pregnancy/hyperthermia guidance.

headline: Severe dry and wet sauna exposures produced comparable heat strain after 20 minutes.
implication: Supports conservative duration guidance and individualized exit before discomfort in high heat/humidity contexts.
caveat: The dry-sauna humidity was high and conditions were described as severe; do not directly translate the 10-min warning to all Finnish sauna use.

headline: Heat/cold review helps keep Finnish sauna distinct from contrast-therapy claims.
implication: Use for modality boundary and mechanism language; do not promote cold-exposure evidence into dry-sauna claims.
caveat: Narrative physiology review, not a protocol-specific trial.

headline: Narrative review supports general Finnish-sauna tolerability but emphasizes weak study designs.
implication: Useful for safety framing around stable chronic disease and medication-related orthostatic hypotension, not as standalone efficacy proof.
caveat: Many underlying studies were uncontrolled and sauna-accustomed; do not generalize to unstable cardiovascular disease or beginners without caution.

headline: Extreme repeated sauna exposure changed endocrine markers and produced transient amenorrhea in five of seven women.
implication: Use to justify conservative dose limits and menstrual-cycle safety cautions.
caveat: The exposure was one hour twice daily for seven days, far above the Murph default protocol.

headline: The sauna and body fluid balance — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use only as a source-owned hydration and fluid-loss safety boundary; do not turn it into an efficacy claim.
caveat: Older source; detailed quantitative estimates were not available in the local batch artifacts.; Not a controlled test of the Murph 3x/week protocol.

headline: Heating mode changed cerebral blood-flow response at thermal tolerance.
implication: Supports stop rules and modality-disambiguation language for heat exposure.
caveat: The sauna condition was hot humid air and heating was to tolerance or core 40 °C, beyond ordinary conservative self-experiment dosing.

headline: The sauna and pregnancy — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use as historical context only inside pregnancy safety discussion; do not use it to override conservative current pregnancy guidance.
caveat: Older source and not a modern guideline.; Must be reconciled with later hyperthermia meta-analyses and ACOG/CDC guidance.

headline: Review-level context frames ordinary sauna as tolerable for healthy and stable cardiovascular populations.
implication: Useful for background and safety nuance, especially distinguishing ordinary use from misuse/abuse.
caveat: Narrative review; do not use for quantified efficacy claims or unstable clinical populations.

headline: Young-women hot/cold thermal-stress study is adjacent, not ordinary dry-sauna evidence.
implication: Supports boundary language around cold immersion, long sessions, and fluid-shift-prone body-composition readings.
caveat: No non-heat control, cold-water exposure is part of the intervention, and acute body-composition estimates should not be treated as durable fat-loss evidence.

headline: Suggested limits to the use of the hot tub and sauna by pregnant women — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use as pregnancy heat-limit context only; current conservative guidance should be shown alongside it.
caveat: Older source; hot tub and sauna are combined and not directly equivalent.; Limit proposals are not proof of safety for all users or modern protocols.

headline: Sauna-Induced Body Mass Loss in Young Sedentary Women and Men — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use as hydration/body-mass-loss measurement context, not as efficacy evidence.
caveat: Young sedentary students; acute body-mass proxy rather than clinical dehydration endpoint.; Exposure differs from 15-20 min sessions or 3x/week practice.

headline: Hot-water passive heat therapy improved vascular function and mean arterial pressure, but it was not sauna.
implication: Supports blood-pressure and vascular-mechanism plausibility for passive heating while preserving modality boundaries.
caveat: Hot-water immersion, higher frequency, and longer thermal dose differ from Finnish dry sauna.

headline: American College of Sports Medicine position stand. Exertional heat illness during training and competition — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use only for heat-illness screening and post-exercise caution, not for sauna efficacy.
caveat: Exercise heat illness guidance, not passive sauna protocol evidence.; Athlete context may not map to sedentary or clinical users.

headline: Effects of sauna on sperm movement characteristics of normal men measured by computer-assisted sperm analysis — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use as a fertility caution source, especially for people actively trying to conceive; do not infer broad benefit or harm magnitude without the full paper.
caveat: Small/older human semen study; participant count and quantitative effects were not available in the local artifacts.; Male fertility endpoint only; not general sauna efficacy evidence.

headline: IHD narrative review adds clinical cardiovascular context only.
implication: Use for contraindication and clinical-boundary language, not as healthy-user protocol evidence.
caveat: Disease population and narrative design limit directness.

headline: Waon heart-failure review is a clinical sibling-variant guardrail.
implication: Use to separate supervised heart-failure heat therapy from wellness Finnish sauna claims.
caveat: Heart-failure participants and Waon dosing do not match the Murph protocol.

headline: Cardiovascular effects of atenolol, scopolamine and their combination on healthy men in Finnish sauna baths — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use as a narrow medication-interaction finding; do not infer all anticholinergic/beta-blocker combinations are safe in sauna.
caveat: Healthy men only.; Specific drugs and doses; not generalizable to frail, older, cardiovascular-disease, or polypharmacy populations.

headline: CVD/PAD heat-therapy review is adjacent clinical context.
implication: Use for clinical boundary language and source recall, not for healthy-user Finnish-sauna efficacy claims.
caveat: CVD/PAD populations and broader heat-therapy modalities do not match the Murph protocol.

headline: Heat-stress consensus supports gradual acclimatization, hydration, cooling, and emergency planning.
implication: Useful for sauna safety operations and adaptation logic, but not direct sauna efficacy evidence.
caveat: Exercise-heat guidance in athletes differs from passive sauna exposure.

headline: Sauna-specific semen-quality harm was not confirmed, but genital heat remains a fertility boundary.
implication: Use cautious reproductive-health safety wording without asserting confirmed sauna harm.
caveat: Not an efficacy source and not specific to the Murph protocol.

headline: Far-infrared sauna review defines a sibling modality boundary.
implication: Use to keep infrared evidence separate from Finnish dry-sauna protocol claims.
caveat: Far-infrared therapy is not the Murph Finnish dry-sauna protocol.

headline: The effect of a single sauna exposure on spermatozoa — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use only as fertility safety context; do not infer long-term fertility outcomes.
caveat: Older single-exposure study; exact sample size/effect estimates not extracted.; Does not represent repeated 3x/week protocol.

headline: FIR review supplies terminology for infrared-sauna boundary claims.
implication: Use to prevent conflating FIR radiation mechanisms with Finnish dry-sauna exposure.
caveat: Not direct human Finnish dry-sauna protocol evidence.

headline: Effects of heat exposure in a Finnish sauna on the pharmacokinetics and metabolism of midazolam — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use as medication-interaction context; do not claim broad sedative safety or risk magnitude without full effect estimates.
caveat: Very small sample of healthy young men.; Specific sedative drug; not generalizable to all CNS depressants or clinical patients.

headline: The sauna, skin and skin diseases — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use for skin-condition cautions and symptom monitoring, not as a claim that sauna treats skin disease.
caveat: Older narrative review; no standardized Murph protocol.; Condition-specific details require full article review before individual guidance.

headline: Regular sauna users showed skin-barrier differences in an exploratory controlled study.
implication: Useful for skin tolerability and hydration-context logging.
caveat: Regular-user comparisons can be confounded, and skin physiology is not a primary Murph outcome.

headline: Differential effects of sauna-, diuretic-, and exercise-induced hypohydration — safety-only appraisal
implication: Use for hydration mechanism/safety context; avoid simple equivalence between sauna dehydration and exercise/diuretic dehydration.
caveat: Older acute physiology study; sample size not extracted.; Hypohydration comparisons are mechanism/safety context rather than a protocol trial.

headline: Sauna Society distinguishes traditional Finnish sauna humidity control from very-low-humidity dry sauna.
implication: Helps define modality boundaries and avoid implying that all Finnish sauna practice is fully dry.
caveat: Educational guidance only; no participant outcomes or efficacy data.

headline: North American Sauna Society build guidance gives temperature and construction safety guardrails.
implication: Useful for implementation safety in home or community sauna contexts.
caveat: Design guidance is not clinical evidence; jurisdictional standards vary.

headline: North American Sauna Society FAQ supports wet/dry humidity context and typical 2–3x/week use.
implication: Useful operational context for Finnish-sauna modality and frequency framing.
caveat: FAQ guidance is not primary evidence and should not be used for efficacy claims.
